% Fixture: mixed-page-sizes
% Four pages with different MediaBoxes and orientations:
%   1. A4 portrait            595.28 x 841.89 pt
%   2. A4 landscape           841.89 x 595.28 pt (a real landscape MediaBox)
%   3. US Letter portrait     612    x 792    pt
%   4. US Letter portrait MediaBox with /Rotate 90 (pdflscape), so a viewer
%      shows it as 792 x 612 pt with the text running left to right.
% KOMA-Script's typearea changes the paper size between pages
% (\KOMAoptions + \recalctypearea; pagesize writes the PDF page size).
\documentclass[10pt,paper=a4,pagesize,DIV=12]{scrartcl}
\input{fixture-common}
\usepackage{pdflscape}
\usepackage{tikz}
\pagestyle{plain}

\begin{document}

% ------------------------------------------------------------------- page 1
\section{A portrait A4 page}

This first page uses the international A4 size in portrait orientation. It
is the most common page size for papers written outside North America, and
the size that most layout code implicitly assumes.

A reader that computes page offsets from the first page alone will place
every later page of this document in the wrong position, because none of the
following pages has the same dimensions as this one.

\clearpage
% ------------------------------------------------------------------- page 2
\KOMAoptions{paper=landscape}
\recalctypearea
\section{A landscape A4 page}

This second page is wider than it is tall. Wide tables and large diagrams
are often set on such pages in appendices and supplementary material.

\begin{center}
  \begin{tikzpicture}[x=10mm,y=10mm]
    \draw (0,0) rectangle (22,4);
    \foreach \x in {2,6,10,14,18} \draw (\x,0.5) rectangle (\x+2,3.5);
  \end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

The page keeps its landscape shape in the file itself, so no rotation is
needed to display it the right way up.

\clearpage
% ------------------------------------------------------------------- page 3
\KOMAoptions{paper=letter,paper=portrait}
\recalctypearea
\section{A portrait US Letter page}

This third page uses the North American letter size, which is slightly
wider and shorter than A4. Documents assembled from several sources often
mix the two sizes without anyone noticing.

\clearpage
% ------------------------------------------------------------------- page 4
\begin{landscape}
\section{A rotated letter page}

This fourth page is stored as a portrait letter page with a rotation of
ninety degrees, the way many tools produce landscape pages. Its text runs
along the long edge of the paper once the rotation is applied.

The width and height reported for this page therefore depend on whether the
rotation is taken into account.
\end{landscape}

\end{document}
